titulo.texto: Married Couple from Ixtlán del Río

frase_gancho.texto: A clay couple, seated side by side, still together after two thousand years.

puente_narrativo.texto: From figures full of detail, we move on to abstraction. Look for a small green stone figure of very simple lines: a rectangle, a triangular nose, and two strokes for a face.

guion_corto.texto: These two clay figures come from Ixtlán del Río, in Nayarit, and measure between forty-eight and fifty-two centimeters. They represent a man and a woman seated next to each other, with faces and arms painted with lines and dots. Notice the jewelry: rings in the ears and the nose, and a conical helmet on the man. The woman rests her hands on her swollen belly. Both are very expressive, like most figures in the Nayarit style. They were made about two thousand years ago and were found in Shaft Tombs. They are thought to represent the ancestors of a lineage, or the founders of a community: two people who, together, ensured the continuity of the family.

guion_largo.texto:
Some works impress us with their monumentality, and others with their tenderness. This couple belongs to the second kind. Two people seated side by side, as if waiting for something together. They have been waiting for more than two thousand years.

They come from Ixtlán del Río, in Nayarit, a region where many shaft tombs have been explored. The Nayarit style is unmistakable: large, hollow figures with very expressive faces, almost portraits, and with lots of color. There are couples, mothers with their children, elders, warriors, and musicians. After the [Jalisco warrior](mna_s10_guerrero_jalisco) and the [dogs of Colima](mna_s10_perros_colima), this couple completes the picture of the three regions of the Shaft Tombs.

Who are they? Several answers have been proposed. The founders of a lineage, venerated ancestors, or simply the deceased buried in the tomb. What we can see is that they are together, and that both wear jewelry of high rank. In the Mesoamerican world, the union of the masculine and the feminine was a way of understanding the balance of the world. You already saw a similar idea in the [mask of duality](mna_s03_mascara_dualidad) from Tlatilco, with its face divided into two halves.

Look at the jewelry. The rings that hang from the ears and the nose indicate high rank. In the West, shell and, later, metal were worked, and they were a sign of prestige. The man’s conical helmet and the woman’s braided hairstyles also tell us how important they were.

Now the paint. Parallel lines, dots, and diagonals in white and ochre cover faces and arms. We do not know what they meant, but in many societies body paint told which group a person belonged to and what role they had. As in the [Teenager of Tamuín](mna_s08_adolescente_huasteco), the body is a page that speaks.

That region holds another secret. Near Ixtlán del Río there is a site called Los Toriles, with a circular temple dedicated to Ehécatl, the god of wind. He is the same god of the cut conch shell in the museum’s courtyard and of the duck-bill mask. His cult reached this place, long after these figures were made.

There is another famous couple in the West, the “lovers of Nayarit,” who embrace. This one does not embrace, but it shares their spirit: the idea that life, even after death, is lived in company. Whoever placed them together in the tomb did not want anyone to be left alone.

There is something that hurts a little. Many figures like these came from looted tombs, and so we know less about their context than we would like. The few that were found intact, with their offering around them, are worth their weight in gold: they tell us who was accompanied by what, and how the dead were bid farewell.

To finish, a technical detail. These figures are hollow and thin-walled, and they stand about half a meter tall. Keeping them from cracking in the kiln demanded a great deal of practice. It is a sign of how much the potters of Nayarit knew.

texto.Culture: Shaft Tomb Tradition / Nayarit (Ixtlán del Río style)
texto.Material: Polychrome clay (ceramic) with geometric face and body paint, ring ornaments in the ears and nose, and modeled headdresses

texto.pregunta: Myth: In ancient Mexico, only powerful men were portrayed.
texto.respuesta: Reality: In the West there are many figures of women, couples, and mothers with children. Here, a woman shares the same rank as her partner.
